question: Should an AI agent ever be allowed to move our money, and if so, under what limits?
reflection: Drawing clear lines around what machines may do with our savings protects trust, and trust is what lets useful tools spread.

AI's Chip Designs Still Have a Few Bugs

one_line: Banks and scientists are setting firmer limits on what AI agents may touch, while AI tools for chip design and biology show promise but still make many mistakes.

top_stories.title: JPMorgan keeps outside agents out of customer accounts
top_stories.what: JPMorgan Chase says outside AI agents may not log in with customer credentials or act inside retail accounts, though limited read-only data sharing through approved connectors is allowed.
top_stories.why: Banks are setting the first practical rules on agent access to money, a template for consent design in other sectors.

top_stories.title: Scientists ask labs to keep cyber-capable AI offline
top_stories.what: An open letter signed by 420 scientists calls for AI models able to carry out cyberattacks to be cut off from the internet by default, with an international body to set containment standards.
top_stories.why: Containment standards could shape how public bodies are allowed to deploy the most capable models.

top_stories.title: AI chip design helps but is far from reliable
top_stories.what: A new benchmark from NVIDIA and ChipAgents found the best AI agent solved only about 17% of full chip-design tasks, even though AI is said to have halved typical design cycles.
top_stories.why: A clear example that AI speeds expert work without replacing expert checking, a useful message for any client adopting AI.

saudi_lens.text: Saudi banks and the central bank are expanding open banking, so JPMorgan's read-only versus act-on-behalf split is a timely reference for agent access rules.

idea.title: Trust in money-handling agents survey
idea.pitch: Survey bank customers on which financial tasks they would let an AI agent do, from viewing balances to paying bills, and what safeguards would change their answer.
idea.first_step: List eight financial tasks in order of risk and draft one trust question per task.

idea_kids.title: Piggy bank rules game
idea_kids.pitch: Children run a pretend shop with paper money and decide which jobs a helper may do alone and which need a grown-up's yes.
idea_kids.first_step: Make paper coins and six task cards, such as counting coins or buying a toy.
